title: When a remote site goes dark, what do you lose?

scenes.headline: When a remote site goes dark, what do you lose?
scenes.voice: Picture a remote site at two in the morning. The grid fails, and the backup supply does not start.

scenes.headline: No power. No cameras. No alarm.
lines: The link to base goes down
scenes.voice: The cameras stop recording, and the link back to base goes down with them. Whatever happens next leaves no evidence, and nobody knows until the morning shift arrives.

scenes.headline: It is not the outage. It is what you cannot prove.
scenes.voice: The real loss is not the outage itself. It is the stock you cannot account for, the incident you cannot investigate, and the question from the board that you cannot answer.

scenes.headline: Remove the single points of failure.
items: Backup power for cameras and recorders
A second link to the control room
scenes.voice: Layered design removes those single points of failure. Backup power for cameras and recorders, a second link to the control room, and alarms that escalate as soon as anything drops.

scenes.headline: Request an executive briefing
scenes.voice: FOG Technologies Nexus designs remote sites that stay visible. Request an executive briefing, and write to CEO at fogtechnexus.space.
